long_synopsis: In the week ending December 26, 2025, the Democracy Clock moved by only one-tenth of a minute, but that stillness masked eighteen distinct trait shifts, almost all toward erosion. The Justice Department missed a legal deadline on Epstein files, released heavily redacted records, disappeared and restored documents, then claimed to have found over a million more pages. Immigration enforcement expanded through a $170 billion buildout, record detention, and plans for 80,000-person facilities. Courts pushed back repeatedly, blocking National Guard deployment and coercive funding cuts. Congress showed split instincts, forcing votes while leadership limited scrutiny. Press freedom faced new pressure as Trump called the New York Times a national security threat and CBS pulled a vetted segment. The week's danger lay in its quietness.
